newsitem.title: UK: Major's Brents pose riddle for firm N.Sea crudes.
newsitem.headline: Major's Brents pose riddle for firm N.Sea crudes.

text.p: North Sea wet crudes were offered at firm values but most buyers held back in morning discussion amid uncertainty over the fate of five July Brents held by a European major, traders said.
Paper was talked weaker in slow trade while outright values were unchanged in featureless business.
An Oseberg loading around July 17 changed hands at Dated Brent +15 and the buyer immediately sold it on at Dated Brent +16, slightly firmer than Thursday's traded value of Dated Brent +14 cents.
Forties was assessed unchanged at around Dated +20/30 on Friday.
"The numbers look quite steamy," said one wet crude trader.
"Yesterday's values indicate short-term support for this market but obviously there is disagreement on how strong it should be," said another trader.
The major background support for physical values remains the lingering riddle of when Iraq will resume exports under the U.N. "oil-for-food" programme.
An Iraqi officials said this week Baghdad would refuse to resume exports until the remaining $800 million of revenue from the first 180 days of the U.N. deal has been spent on humanitarian supplies.
Good demand inspired partly by concern over the future of the Iraqi exports lifted differentials in trades of Forties, Oseberg, Ekofisk and Troll on Thursday.
"But in the short term the important question is what the (major Brent holder) is up to. It's a very unclear picture," said one analyst.

Traders heard talk the European major would try to load his Brents on a ULCC to the United States if the arb recovered to economic levels. But others said this looked improbable as long as the arb languished at thin values.
Traders also heard talk another major will try to load a VLCC of Oseberg to Asia.
Brent Contracts for Differences continued to slide, with this week discussed at August Brent -33/-30 cents. Next week (June 30-July 4) declined to -37/-33 cents.
Fifteen-day intermonth spreads were mixed. July/August was valued at around -16 cents, with August/September around +17 cents.
